row.evidence: DeepL's pricing page lists 'User provisioning (SCIM)' first in the Business plan (€49.99 per user/month, billed annually), while Team (€24.99) gets SSO; the help centre says SCIM is for those subscriptions 'with 50 users or more'.
row.notes: Status unchanged (gated): SCIM is a higher-tier feature (Business, plus legacy Ultimate, Enterprise and Voice plans) and needs at least 50 users; SSO starts on Team. Plans were renamed since June (Starter/Advanced/Ultimate -> Individual/Team/Business/Enterprise). The pricing page served EUR prices (Germany) from our location and no USD price could be loaded, so per-user USD fields are null and June's USD figures ($8.74 / $57.49, 6.6x) were dropped; in EUR, Business is 2.0x Team. SCIM base URL https://scim.deepl.com with the SCIM admin API key as bearer token; Okta (SAML custom app only), Entra (non-gallery app) and OneLogin (generic SCIM Provisioner) are documented. Disabling a user unassigns the license; deleting in the IdP deletes the DeepL account and transfers glossaries to the admin. Admins cannot be managed via SCIM. DeepL's Admin API manages API keys and usage, not users.

auth.token_source: DeepL account Settings > Team > User provisioning configuration > Manage user provisioning > Enable SCIM provisioning (creates a SCIM admin API key, also under Admin keys)

deprovision.data_retained: Disabled users stay in the team (default group) with status 'License unassigned'. A user deleted in the IdP is fully deleted in DeepL and their glossaries move to the organisation's admin.

roles.how: IdP groups pushed via SCIM become DeepL product groups (Translator, Write, Voice) that drive license and product assignment; admins cannot be managed via SCIM.

limitations.text: SCIM requires 50 or more users on an eligible subscription.
Admins cannot be managed via SCIM; a SCIM user promoted to Admin can no longer be managed by SCIM.
Okta SCIM works only with a SAML (not OIDC) integration.
Existing accounts outside the organisation cannot be imported; email updates fail with SAML Email NameID format.
Users or groups existing before SCIM that are not assigned in the IdP are not deleted automatically.

user_api.notes: The Admin API covers developer API keys and usage analytics only (and supplies the SCIM key); no user-management endpoints were found in the developer docs index.

okta.notes: DeepL's guide uses a custom SAML 2.0 app integration with SCIM; okta.com/integrations/deepl/ returned 404.

entra.notes: Non-gallery enterprise application per DeepL's SSO guide.

onelogin.notes: Uses OneLogin's generic 'SCIM Provisioner with SAML (SCIM v2 Core)' app.

fallbacks.other_sync: JIT group synchronization over SAML or OIDC (Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin)

searched: help-centre API search: scim, user provisioning, sso
open_questions: USD prices could not be loaded (the pricing page geolocates to EUR and the headless render was blocked); per-user USD values are null.
Whether 'Team' or 'Individual' should be the team plan: Individual (€7.49/month) is single-user, so Team was used.
SCIM filtering, pagination, GET endpoints, ServiceProviderConfig/Schemas and rate limits are not documented.
SCIM admin API key expiry is not documented.
Whether disabling a user via SCIM ends active DeepL sessions is not stated (docs say the IdP denies access at next login).
No Okta OIN, Entra gallery, Google Workspace or JumpCloud catalogue app found.
No audit-log API or user-event webhooks documented.
